title: How do four Junes give one monthly average?
description: A town's June rainfall over four years is added and shared equally among the years to give a monthly average. The video shows that the average is a typical June, not any one real June. It breaks Keeko's doubt that the sum is the average.
teaching_notes: One idea: a monthly average is the sum of the same month over several years, shared equally among the years. Watch for students who give the sum as the average.

source: Suppose a town's June rainfall over 4 years was 820, 900, 76
video_script.why: The child has read rainfall graphs but has not yet seen how one monthly average comes from the same month over many years.
video_script.substitution: Add the same month of each year, then divide by the number of years.
video_script.anchor: the book's graphs of the monthly average rainfall of cities
video_script.wrong_answer: the average June rainfall is three thousand four hundred millimetres
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the four Junes and forgets to share the sum among the four years.
video_script.payoff_line: the average rainfall for June is eight hundred fifty millimetres

final_answer.value: 850 millimetres, the typical June, not any one real June
final_answer.spoken: the average rainfall for June is eight hundred fifty millimetres, a typical June and not any one real June

maths_rules: June rainfall over four years in millimetres: 820, 900, 760, 920
none of the four Junes had exactly 850 millimetres: the average is a typical June, not a real one
slip: 3400 is the rain of four Junes together, not of one June
video_script.design: One idea: add the same month over the years, then share equally. The wrong idea is that the sum is the average. Four rain bars for the four Junes stay on screen; they are pooled and then shared into four equal bars.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Suppose a town's June rainfall over four years was eight hundred twenty millimetres, then nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The next two Junes gave seven hundred sixty and nine hundred twenty millimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the monthly average rainfall for June in this town?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko appears at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the four bars poured into one tall pile, then shared into four equal bars

marks.same: the four June bars are lit and the other months are dimmed
marks.pool: the four bars are poured into one tall pile
marks.share: the pile is shared into four equal bars

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Rainfall is collected for the same month over several years.
<bookmark mark='pool'/>The rain of all those Junes is added together into one pile.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Then the pile is shared equally among the years. One share is the monthly average.

beats.on_screen: Given: June rainfall over 4 years: 820, 900, 760, 920 millimetres

marks.given: the four values are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the June rainfall of four years, in millimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the monthly average rainfall for June

marks.find: the task is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the monthly average rainfall for June.

marks.add: the four values are joined by plus signs

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, add the four Junes. Eight hundred twenty, plus nine hundred, plus seven hundred sixty, plus nine hundred twenty.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The sum is three thousand four hundred.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: average = sum / number of years = 3400 / 4

marks.div: the sum is written over the number of years, 4

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step two, share the sum equally among the four years.
Divide three thousand four hundred by four.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 850 millimetres, a typical June and not any one real June

marks.typ: the four real Junes are shown next to the average, and none of them equals it

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The average rainfall for June is eight hundred fifty millimetres.
<bookmark mark='typ'/>It is a typical June, and not any one real June. None of the four Junes had exactly that rain.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the pile and the four bars
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the tall pile struck out as one June; the pile shared into four equal bars, one of them lit

marks.doubt: the tall pile is labelled one June
marks.four: the label is struck out and the pile is shown as four Junes together
marks.share: the pile is shared into four equal bars and one bar is lit

beats.removed: the label one June is struck out
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the average June rainfall is three thousand four hundred millimetres. That is what the Junes gave.
<bookmark mark='four'/>But that is the rain of four Junes together, not of one June.
<bookmark mark='share'/>To get one typical June, we share the pile among the four years.
